findings.verifierReasoning: The 75% cash-consideration and fair-value requirement is explicit, unambiguous, fully-supported source text (not dependent on any missing schedule for its baseline meaning - the schedule is only a carve-out FROM this requirement). The proposed IR, however, collapses the entire condition's 'expression' field into kind UNSUPPORTED, with the stated reason being solely that Schedule 6.05 (the narrow exception) is unavailable. This conflates a fully-known, fully-supported quantitative threshold (75% cash consideration) with an unrelated, genuinely-unknown carve-out, and as a result the 75% figure never appears anywhere in the IR as a structured/computable value (confirmed by the deterministic signal that PERCENT 0.75 does not appear anywhere in the compiled IR). A downstream compliance check relying on this IR's structured expression would have no way to verify the baseline 75% cash-consideration requirement on the (k) basket - a basket that can be quite large (greater of $25,000,000 or 25% of Applicable EBITDA) - because the requirement was effectively discarded as 'unsupported' rather than represented with only the schedule carve-out flagged as a gap.

findings.verifierReasoning: The 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' proviso grammatically refers back to everything stated above it in §6.05, which includes both the asset-disposition prohibition AND the equity-issuance prohibition (both are introduced by the same 'except:' clause). Because the proviso's substantive content is truncated and unknown, it is equally plausible that it further restricts the equity-issuance permission (e.g., restricting issuances of Equity Interests of a Borrower or similar) as it is that it only restricts asset dispositions. The proposed IR treats this uncertainty as material enough to downgrade r1 to PARTIAL but treats r2 as COMPLETE with no corresponding disclosure, which is an internally inconsistent application of the same known evidentiary gap and could overstate confidence in the equity-issuance rule's completeness.

findings.sourceEvidence: No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, Dispose of any asset... nor will any Loan Party permit any Restricted Subsidiary to issue any additional Equity Interest in such Restricted Subsidiary...
findings.verifierReasoning: The covenant's substantive restriction is not limited to actions taken directly by Loan Parties - it also directly restricts the conduct of Restricted Subsidiaries (dispositions of assets and issuances of Equity Interests), with the Loan Party covenant structured as a 'will not permit' obligation over those Restricted Subsidiaries. If entityScope is used downstream to determine which entities' transactions are checked against this rule, limiting it to LOAN_PARTY alone risks a Restricted Subsidiary's disposition or equity issuance not being flagged against this covenant at all, which would materially change a compliance conclusion. This may be an intentional schema convention (scoping to the obligated party rather than the acting party), so I flag this as uncertain rather than definitively material, but it warrants review.
